initial_prompts.A:
Create a premium original scientific paper Fig.1 concept schematic, not a poster, using the three attached reference images solely as visual design guidance. Landscape wide high-resolution white background; refined technical illustration, elegant thin outlines, modern Arial-like short English labels, generous whitespace, pale lavender optical channel, muted blue electrical-weight channel, champagne-gold contacts and charcoal typography. Subtle isometric device depth and transparent signal planes are desirable. Scientific content MUST follow these author specifications, NEVER the unrelated mechanisms in references: GaON/GaN photomemristive sensor in a 2TG1C1S pixel array. S encodes light history into VOLATILE photoconductance G. C separately stores capacitor voltage V_C as electrical weight. TG1 controls weight writing; TG2 enables readout. During sensing sensor externally applied voltage =0, light pulses accumulate G and G decays in dark. Weight writing TG1 ON and TG2 OFF: fixed V_in plus variable t_write gives stored V_C; it does NOT reprogram G. Readout TG1 OFF and TG2 ON applies NONZERO capacitor voltage to S; I_ij(t_r)≈G_ij(t_r)V_C,ij(t_r), assuming approximately ohmic short readout and small capacitor droop. Optical conductance matrix G and voltage template V_C^(k) BOTH ENTER one ⊙ node (Hadamard multiplication), THEN products enter Σ node, THEN ONE scalar current I_out^(k). Do not draw weight matrix after multiplication or connect it only to Σ. One template→one scalar; changing templates gives successive independent scalar outputs. No direct scalar→multi-class plot. Show noisy repeated T-shirt input frames, array, internal grayscale G matrix (NOT acquired readout image), separate blue weight matrix, multiplication, summation, scalar output. Four schematic response traces share time: optical pulses only in sensing, G rises cumulatively during light and decays between and afterwards; V_read=0 in sensing and has differing positive pulses in readout; I pulses exactly align with V_read and reflect decaying G and voltage, no measurements/ticks. Traces BLACK, sensing background pale lavender and readout pale blue. Label 'Schematic'. No nonvolatile optical memory claims, no band diagrams, no reservoir energy landscapes, no unsupported detailed TG circuit, no fabricated experimental values, no performance or energy claims, no logos. Short clear labels, critical scientific arrows correct. This is an internal concept draft pending author review.
COMPOSITION A: One visually commanding large isometric GaON/GaN sensor chip at center-left occupying about a third of the image, fine gold peripheral pads, crisp lavender pixel array; stacked noisy T-shirt input frames on far left project a subtle lavender optical wedge onto chip. To chip's right upper-middle float an internal grayscale G map; below it a clearly separate blue capacitor weight matrix supplied by a small write-time to capacitor icon. Both matrices feed one clearly positioned ⊙ node, then Σ and scalar current. Rightmost quarter contains elegant four synchronized black response traces. Put compact TG1/TG2 write/read mode badges under main chip. Visual hierarchy: chip hero first, states second, math/output third. A sophisticated editorial schematic with depth, not flat boxes, approximately 16:9. Title 'Optical history meets voltage-weighted computing'.

COMPOSITION B: Three functional zoom bands arranged vertically to right of a tall beautiful isometric sensor array hero on the left (30% of width). Fine colored leader lines connect chip regions to bands. Top lavender band: 'Zero-bias temporal sensing', stacked noisy T-shirt frames, accumulation/decay mini-trace and internal G state. Middle blue band: 'Capacitor weight storage', fixed V_in / variable t_write → capacitor → blue V_C template, badges TG1 ON / TG2 OFF. Bottom neutral/purple-blue band: 'Weighted readout and summation', miniature G and V matrices enter separate branches of ⊙ -> Σ -> one I_out^(k), badge TG1 OFF / TG2 ON. Use a small inset with four aligned black schematic traces in open area at far right spanning top two bands if it fits; prioritize clear legible layout. Bands are elegant light-tint regions with restrained thin borders, not busy dashed rectangles. Do NOT add energy band diagrams or nonvolatile states from reference. Isometric chip, magnified pixel abstraction S and C as distinct elements without invented wiring. About 16:10. Title 'One pixel, two states, weighted computation'.
